# A Site and One Brand {#sec-sites}



The evaluation now has a report, a model card and a deck, in three formats each, scattered
across a folder. Investors, a client's risk team and a new colleague will each want the
latest version, from one address, and they will judge the work partly by whether it looks
like it came from one place. A small team has no designer for that. It has a site, built from
the same sources, and one file that says what the company's colours, type and logo are, which
every format then follows.

This chapter makes the evaluation a website with a home page, an About page and search, gives
it one brand that every format follows, and checks every page with a script.

::: opener
- Say what one brand file reaches in Quarto, and how Word and PowerPoint get the same look.
- Ask for a website from an existing project: a render list, a navbar, a footer, a home page
  with a listing, an About page and social cards.
- Check every page of a site for alt text, titles, descriptions, heading order and contrast
  with a script.
- Decide where a branded site may be published, and what to set before it is.

Start from
: your `acme-eval` repository at the end of @sec-slides, or `checkpoints/16-eval-slides/`.

You build
: `_brand.yml` and a logo, Word and PowerPoint templates made from it, and a site of
  five pages, with a check script.

Checkpoint
: `checkpoints/17-eval-site/`
:::

## One brand, every format {#sec-sites-brand-reach}

A *brand file*, `_brand.yml`, states a company's look once: a palette of named colours, the
roles they play (background, foreground, primary), the fonts, and the logo. Quarto reads it
and applies it, but not to every format. Which formats it reaches decides how you build the
rest:

| Format | What `_brand.yml` gives it |
|---|---|
| Web pages, sites and dashboards | colours and the navbar's logo; fonts on web pages |
| Reveal.js decks | colours, fonts and the logo on each slide |
| Typst PDFs | page and text colours, heading fonts, the logo |
| Word and PowerPoint | nothing: each gets a *reference document*, made from the brand by a script |

: Where one brand file reaches, in Quarto 1.10.20. {#tbl-sites-brand}

So the plan is one source of truth with two routes out of it: Quarto applies the brand where it
can, and a short script turns the same file into the two templates where it cannot. Change a
colour in `_brand.yml`, rerun the script, render, and every format follows.

## The brand file {#sec-sites-brand}

The brand file starts from the deck's theme: the same colours, now in one place that every
format reads.

::: {.prompt .long}
```default
Add _brand.yml with Acme's colours from acme.scss as a palette and the roles primary, background and foreground, system fonts, and a logo at brand/logo.svg (a wordmark; say in a comment the company is fictional). Make slides.qmd use it (theme: [default, acme.scss, brand]), move every colour out of acme.scss, and make tests/test_deck_contrast.py read the colours from _brand.yml. Render the deck and the report, run the tests, and tell me where the brand's colours appear in each output.
```
:::

::: {.agent}
writes `_brand.yml` and `brand/logo.svg` · edits `acme.scss`, `slides.qmd` and the test · renders · `uv run pytest`
:::

The brand's text colours are the theme's of @tbl-slides-contrast, now read from `_brand.yml`,
and the same test checks them: it now reads the file that is the source of truth, not a copy
of it. Verify where the brand landed, as the prompt asks: in the site's or deck's CSS, the
colours appear as variables; in a Typst PDF, they set the page and the headings.

## Word and PowerPoint, in the same colours {#sec-sites-templates}

Word and PowerPoint take their look from a reference document (@sec-slides-pptx). Make both
from the brand with one script, so that a change of colour reaches them too:

::: {.prompt .long}
```default
Turn scripts/make_pptx_reference.py into scripts/make_reference_docs.py, which also makes templates/acme-reference.docx from Quarto's default reference.docx with the brand's colours and font (in its theme and its Title and Heading styles). Use it as the docx `reference-doc` of report.qmd and model-card.qmd, render both, and check the colours in the Word files.
```
:::

The check is in the Word file, a zip of XML: its theme's and its styles' colours must be the
brand's. Quarto's default document colours headings and links from its own theme's accent, and
the title not at all, so the script writes the brand's colours into those styles. Check the
file, not the script; and check a Word file in Word, and in whatever your readers open it with.

| What you see | The fix |
|---|---|
| Sass stops: "Undefined variable" | `brand` last in the deck's `theme:` list |
| Typst warns "unknown font family" | no generic `sans-serif` in the brand's fonts |
| Charts ignore the brand | a helper gives matplotlib the brand's ink and paper |
| The new template cannot be committed | except it in `.gitignore`: `!templates/*.docx` |

: Met while testing the brand and its templates, 2026-11-18. {#tbl-sites-traps}

## A site from the project {#sec-sites-site}

A Quarto *website* is a project whose `_quarto.yml` lists its pages and how to navigate them.
Everything else on a modern site is vocabulary you can ask for:

| Ask for | Quarto calls it |
|---|---|
| exactly these pages | an explicit `render:` list |
| a menu with the logo | `navbar:`, whose logo comes from the brand |
| a line on every page | `page-footer:` |
| an About page | `about:` with a template: `jolla`, `trestles`, `solana`, `marquee` or `broadside` |

: A website's pages and navigation (Quarto 1.10.20). {#tbl-sites-vocab}

| Ask for | Quarto calls it |
|---|---|
| a home page that lists the documents | a *listing*, `type: table`, `default` or `grid` |
| search | on by default; `search.json` in `_site/` |
| cards when a link is shared | *social cards*: `open-graph: true`, with `site-url` and a `description` on each page |
| the other formats of a page | Quarto's "Other formats" links (`format-links`) |

: How a website is found and shared. {#tbl-sites-find}

::: {.prompt .long}
```default
Make this folder a Quarto website: _quarto.yml with an explicit render list (index.qmd, about.qmd, report.qmd, model-card.qmd, slides.qmd), execute-dir project, a navbar with the brand's logo, a page footer with the fictional-company notice and the data's CC BY 4.0 credit, site-url https://example.org/acme-eval/, open-graph, and a description on every page. Render the site and list the pages and any warnings.
```
:::

::: {.agent}
writes `_quarto.yml` · adds descriptions · `uv run quarto render` → `_site/`
:::

::: {.prompt}
```default
Write index.qmd: a first sentence stating the headline result as inline code with a guard, then a table listing of the three documents. Write about.qmd: an about page with the trestles template. Render the site and tell me what the home page's first sentence says.
```
:::

::: {.agent}
writes `index.qmd` and `about.qmd` · `uv run quarto render` → `_site/`
:::

::: {.you}
`uv run quarto preview` · open the address it prints, and the site on a phone-sized window
:::

The home page's first sentence is the headline, computed and guarded like any other: in the
finished site, v3 is named as the release that ranks best, with its numbers read
from `outputs/`. Its description, written once in the page's front matter, feeds the listing
on the home page, the search index, the page's `<meta>` tag and the card a chat app shows when
someone pastes the link. So write one sentence per page, without numbers, because a
description is front matter and cannot compute.

`site-url` is a placeholder until you know where the site will live; set it before publishing,
because social cards need absolute addresses for their images.

::: pitfall
Once the folder is a website, every render writes into `_site/`, a single file's too, so
scripts that expected `slides.html` beside the source must look in `_site/`. The deck's PDF
and alt-text scripts failed until they did.
:::

::: story
<!-- source: book/chapters/sites.qmd lines 215-217 at 651db10 ("a navbar in the brand's
primary colour hid a logo in the same navy; `background: light` in the navbar fixed it") -->
In the test run of this chapter, the navbar took the brand's primary colour, a navy. The
logo was the same navy, so the bar hid it. `background: light` in the navbar fixed it. A
build log reports what was written, not what can be seen: look at the site, not only its
log.
:::

## Checks for every page {#sec-sites-checks}

A person checks the page they are looking at. A script checks every page, every time. Ask for
the checks a site most often fails, as code:

::: {.prompt}
```default
Write scripts/check_site.py: after a render, check every page in _site/ for alt text on every image, a lang attribute, a title, a description meta tag and no skipped heading levels, and that the brand's text colours have a contrast of at least 4.5:1 on its background. Run it and fix what it finds.
```
:::

::: think
`check_site.py` passes on every page. Name one thing it has proved on all of them, and one
thing only your eyes can check.

Proved: every image has alt text, every page a title, a description and a language, no heading
level is skipped, and the brand's text colours pass 4.5:1. Not proved: that the alt text is
true, that the logo can be seen on its bar, that the page reads well on a phone. A script
checks every page for what can be stated as a rule; you check one page for everything else.
:::

The checker's first run found two problems, both on the deck's page. Reveal.js showed the
brand's logo with no alt text, until `_brand.yml` gave it one, and wrote no description tag,
until a short filter added it from the page's `description`. Neither shows on the screen;
both are what the script is for. Each check is a common failure:

- **Alt text** is what a screen reader announces in place of an image (@sec-md-link-image).
- **A language** tells a screen reader how to pronounce the page.
- **A title and a description** are what a search result and a shared link show.
- **Headings that skip a level** confuse anyone who navigates by headings.
- **Contrast** is the rule of @sec-slides-theme, applied to the whole brand.

The script does not replace looking at the site, or a full audit such as Lighthouse's
accessibility score; it catches the regressions that a new page or a new colour would
otherwise slip in.

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/17-eval-site/README.md
```
:::

## Where a branded site may go {#sec-sites-publish}

The site is static files in `_site/`, published like the London guide's (@sec-london-publish),
to any of the hosts of @sec-hosting. Two decisions come first. **Who may see it.** A public
evaluation of a public dataset can go on any public host; an evaluation of a client's data
needs a host your organisation approves. **Where it lives**, so that `site-url` can be set and
the social cards work.

::: tryit
Build the brand, the templates, the site and the check script, and preview the site.

::: done
one `_brand.yml` sets the colours of the site, the deck and the PDFs; the Word and PowerPoint
files are in the same colours; `check_site.py` reports no problems; and the home page's first
sentence names the best release.
:::
:::

## Summary {.unnumbered}

::: keyideas
- One `_brand.yml` sets colours, fonts and the logo for web pages, Reveal.js decks, Typst PDFs
  and dashboards; Word and PowerPoint get them through reference documents a script makes from
  the same file.
- A website is a project: an explicit render list, a navbar, a footer, a listing home page, an
  About page, search, and a description on every page that feeds listings, search and social
  cards.
- Descriptions are front matter and cannot compute: write them without numbers.
- Check every page with a script (alt text, language, title, description, heading order,
  contrast), and still look at the site.
- Decide who may see a site before choosing where it goes, and set `site-url` before
  publishing.
:::

The last of the evaluation's core outputs is the one that has to stand on its own outside the
company: a technical white paper, with references a reader can check.
